prompt:
Produce ONE complete hyper-realistic integrated illustrated Schemin' 26 Week 11 cinematic memo page. The output is a **finished typeset portrait page**, never a lone visual still, contact sheet, PDF-looking form or prompt illustration. Portrait art may have two to three filmically connected camera beats on this ONE page when necessary for combat continuity; do not create spreadsheet cells or lazy grid borders. Maintain 9:16 framing with a high-quality native page target of 1080x1920 px, plus phone reading at 390x693 px.
ISSUE MASTHEAD (printed exactly once): SCHEMIN’ ’26 • WEEK 11
MAIN HEADLINE: He Was Here Before Us
MATCHUP DECK (printed exactly once): His Majesty’s Blood at D0nkey K0ng
PUBLICATION BODY (PRINT EXACTLY, no deletions or added unsupported facts): Their first collision rang against the lantern stones. Wilson drove his axe down; Austin caught its haft with his sword and turned aside instead of meeting the centaur’s weight head-on. Hooves hammered the narrow deck. Wilson twisted for a second cut, forcing Austin toward the parapet. “He was here before us,” Austin said, glancing at the waiting carter. He slipped inside the next swing and struck Wilson’s armored upper body. The impact shoved the huge warrior backward. His hind hooves crossed on rain-slick stone. All four feet fought for purchase as the parapet rushed toward him.
STORY MOTION: Professional-grade fight logic: impact -> pressure -> sidestep/pivot -> counterstrike -> visible hoof slip. Never invent airborne weapons, disconnected limbs or teleport.
PHYSICAL BEAT SEQUENCE:
C (upper kinetic wedge): An over-shoulder charged contact: Wilson's axe comes down on a visible arc and Austin's ornate sword meets the haft/edge in one coherent plane; shower of sparks is brief and source-motivated. ACTING: Mass and load transfer visible; black armored hooded Austin defends with his actual blade.
D (central large image): Tracking reverse: Wilson rotates ALL FOUR hooves on wet central stones, uses body weight to press, Austin steps laterally toward lamp/reset stone, one boot planted, cloak trails leeward. Carter and cart remain at left approach. ACTING: Combatants physically reposition without swapping places; silhouettes remain legible.
E (lower diagonal payoff): Austin moves inside the axe reach, delivers a decisive armor-thudding sword strike across Wilson's upper guard; Wilson's hind hooves cross/skid and his front hooves scramble near the intact parapet, his body still on deck at cut. ACTING: Austin wins because of a timed counterstrike plus wet traction, not wind magically pushing Wilson. No fall until next page.
CHARACTER CORRECTION ABSOLUTE: Austin Byars is THE BELT KEEPER: COMPLETELY HOODED FACE, TWO LUMINOUS RED EYES, segmented BLACK armor, circular GOLD chest medallion, gold title belt, crimson-black ragged cape, ornate sword. No face, no exposed brown hair, no generic swordsman. This is not a human-faced knight. He cannot have visible ordinary hair or brown human eyes. Reference approved Commissioner October 18 PNG and identity crops. Wilson Look is ONE single gorilla upper torso seamlessly fused to four-legged four-hoof horse/centaur body with red-and-gold Arsenal battle armor and heavy war axe; use current four-hoof Oct18 lineup, not older contradictory biped reference. The carter, horse and canvas wagon remain a grounded working observer at left approach. The SAME intact narrow stone bridge and working lantern as Week 10 physical p33; Mountain Lake is visible on BOTH sides. Rain-glazed center stone reset, working wagon at left approach, both piers readable. No wider invented bridge, no missing cart.
WEATHER: Intense local storm squall: directional crosswind, whipping crimson cape and wagon canopy, leaves, cold rain, large wind-agitated waves hitting piers, loud whitecaps/spray beneath intact span. Founder asks for Wilson to fall into a river of raging water. Atlas presently authorizes the named water body as Mountain Lake; depict *violent churning storm water below the bridge*, record literal directional river/rapid hydrology as an outstanding geography decision rather than silently asserting a new river.
CONTINUITY OUT: Wilson is at edge with weight moving outward, all 4 hooves visible, still not in water; Austin sword held, Belt remains with Austin, bridge intact.
TYPE DESIGN: Atmospheric negative-space typography in the actual cinematic picture. Reading order masthead -> large headline -> matchup -> body -> scene -> coda, with scene-led layout, readable letterforms, not bottom paragraph pasted onto a completed image. Print score only where official result is included in v.print_copy. If image-generation text is unreliable, deterministic compositor overlays exact text, never truncated. No visible page number or F##/P##, no internal gate text and no dated old TheFFHub win probabilities.
REJECT IF: exposed-face Austin, non-centaur Wilson, unearned fall, multiple duplicated independent combatant bodies inside one beat, disconnected axe/sword geometry, floaty physical motion, static standoff, no real charging/combat, visible folio ID, missing dialogue/publication body, unreadable 390px narrative, wrong venue or invented directional river rapids.
